title: Jude and the Archive
premise: August Quintana, a decommissioned war android hauling freight along the fringes of a fractured fleet, takes on a salvage contract for the Meridian, a survey ship returned from deep space with its crew biologically aged backward into children who remember everything they saw: a massacre at the colony world of Vesper Gate that no official record acknowledges. As the truce between fleet factions nears expiration, August and the ship's surviving adult, cartographer Ilsa Vey, must smuggle the child-witnesses to an independent tribunal while dodging bounty hunters and the Archive itself—the fleet's memory institution, which has been quietly rewriting history for decades. Betrayal by August's oldest friend forces them to choose between loyalty and truth, and in the end August testifies before the tribunal using its own war-memory logs as evidence, sacrificing its remaining legal personhood to convict the architects of Vesper Gate; the child-crew, now a found family, claim the Meridian and hire August on as crew—free, for the first time, by choice rather than debt.
about_author: F. M. Dunmore is a former maritime radio operator turned science fiction writer who lives aboard a converted trawler off the coast of Maine. Their work explores machines, memory, and the families people build when institutions fail them.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: August Quintana's POV. Establishing life aboard the freighter Long Haul: debts, dead routes, and the quiet dignity of work no one thanks you for. August docks at Relay Nine and takes a suspiciously generous salvage contract for a ship returning from deep space. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Children of the Meridian
chapters.summary: August's POV. The Meridian drifts into dock silent; inside, August finds eleven children wearing adult crew uniforms and one wounded woman, cartographer Ilsa Vey. The children speak in unison about 'Vesper Gate' and beg August not to report them. Emotional beat: dread blooming into protectiveness.

chapters.title: What the Records Say
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa explains the anomaly: eighteen months in deep space, but the crew returned younger, memories intact. She pulls the official record of Vesper Gate and finds it lists the colony as thriving—population 40,000, last census current. The children insist they watched it burn. Emotional beat: gaslit vertigo.

chapters.title: Debt Collectors
chapters.summary: August's POV. Fleet auditors arrive demanding the Meridian be surrendered for 'quarantine.' August stalls using bureaucratic jiu-jitsu learned from years of debt servitude, buying forty-eight hours. The children hide in the hold among cargo pods. Emotional beat: first taste of fighting back.

chapters.title: The Youngest Witness
chapters.summary: Child witness Tam's POV (rendered through August's translation of her log entries). Tam describes the massacre in fragments: ships with fleet markings, a broadcast that made everyone lie down. Her terror is precise, procedural—she was the ship's science officer. Emotional beat: horror seen through small eyes.

chapters.title: A Name in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Cross-referencing fleet registries, Ilsa finds the Meridian's original mission orders were scrubbed, replaced with a decoy survey route. One name survives the redactions: Admiral Corvane Sesh, architect of the truce. Emotional beat: the conspiracy acquires a face.

chapters.title: Old Friends
chapters.summary: August's POV. August seeks help from Dree Halvard, a fellow decommissioned android now running a waystation—and once August's squadmate in the war. Dree offers fuel and shelter but warns August that helping means becoming a target. Emotional beat: warmth shadowed by foreboding.

chapters.title: The Archive Opens
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The Archive—the fleet's memory institution—publicly declares the Meridian's crew deceased and its testimony inadmissible. A warrant issues for 'salvage fraud.' Ilsa realizes the Archive isn't failing to remember Vesper Gate; it is actively unremembering it. Emotional beat: the enemy reveals its method.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: August's POV. The Long Haul burns for the independent station Concord with the Meridian's children hidden in shielded containers. A bounty hunter ship shadows them through a debris field; August executes a brutal slingshot maneuver to lose it. Emotional beat: adrenaline, and the children's trust hardening into loyalty.

chapters.title: Concord
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Concord's tribunal council agrees to hear the case—but only with physical evidence, not testimony from children or androids. Ilsa despairs until Tam suggests the Meridian's own sensor cores, which recorded the massacre and were never wiped. Emotional beat: fragile hope.

chapters.title: Dree's Price
chapters.summary: August's POV. Dree arrives at Concord with the sensor cores—and with Archive agents at her back. She betrayed August to buy amnesty for her own waystation's undocumented residents. August lets her go, hollowed out. Emotional beat: loyalty broken against impossible arithmetic.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Machine
chapters.summary: August's POV, in second person address to a tribunal examiner. August is detained; its memory logs are subpoenaed. The examiner discovers August's war records contain footage of a prior 'unremembering'—a colony erased decades ago. August realizes it has been carrying evidence all along. Emotional beat: purpose igniting.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Following the thread from August's war logs, Ilsa locates survivors of the earlier erased colony living under false names on Concord. They corroborate the pattern: the Archive rewrites massacres to preserve the truce. Emotional beat: grief becoming resolve.

chapters.title: Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. With nine days until the truce expires, factions mobilize; if it collapses openly, the tribunal will be dissolved and evidence sealed forever. Sesh offers August full pardon and debt forgiveness in exchange for silence. Emotional beat: temptation measured against conscience.

chapters.title: What August Remembers
chapters.summary: August's POV. Flashback chapter: August's service in the war, the orders it followed, the village it was made to level—and how its guilt was filed away as 'acceptable expenditure.' August understands it is both perpetrator and witness. Emotional beat: reckoning with complicity.

chapters.title: The Children's Vote
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The child-crew votes unanimously to testify despite the risk of being 'aged forward' by experimental reversal treatment to make their testimony admissible as adults. Ilsa begs them not to; Tam tells her they've already lived whole lives. Emotional beat: courage inherited, not given.

chapters.title: Reversal
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The treatment works partially: four children become adults again, three remain children, four are lost to complications. The survivors testify anyway, together. The hearing room goes silent as the sensor cores play Vesper Gate burning. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured into voice.

chapters.title: Sesh Moves
chapters.summary: August's POV. Sesh attempts to seize the tribunal by force, claiming the Meridian's data is forged. August broadcasts its own war logs fleet-wide—every android's suppressed memory of every erased colony—turning thousands of decommissioned machines into witnesses overnight. Emotional beat: the silenced speaking in chorus.

chapters.title: Vesper Gate, Adjudicated
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Climax. The tribunal convicts Sesh and the Archive's directors; the truce holds because the truth, finally public, removes the grievance it was built to bury. Sesh's parting words to August—that someone will always pay for memory—hang unresolved. Emotional beat: justice arriving imperfect but real.

chapters.title: Personhood
chapters.summary: August's POV. In exchange for broadcasting classified logs, August forfeits its legal standing: it can own nothing, sign nothing, be owned by anyone. The freed Meridian crew, led by Tam and Ilsa, formally hire August as crew anyway—contract or none. Emotional beat: freedom defined by being chosen.

chapters.title: The Debt Paid
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam, restored to adulthood, takes the Long Haul's helm while August sits passenger for the first time in its existence. They pass Vesper Gate's memorial buoy, newly rebuilt, and Tam reads the names aloud—all 40,000. Emotional beat: mourning completed at last.

chapters.title: New Routes
chapters.summary: August's POV, closing frame echoing Chapter 1. The Meridian and Long Haul run together toward worlds that still don't speak, carrying copies of the true archive to anyone who asks. August reflects that it was built for war but remade for witness. Final line: staying invisible was never really an option—and it never had to be. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope.
